payload.title: M9: Machine code and assembly lessons (machine, assembly, then C)
payload.description: Intent: As the student, I want the first programming lessons to start with machine code, then move up to assembly, then to C, so that I understand what the computer actually does before using higher-level languages. Includes: a teaching instruction set with an emulator, an assembler and disassembler, Monaco language support (syntax highlighting, hover docs, error markers) for both machine code and assembly, a stepping view (registers, memory, program counter, flags) in the IDE, runnable examples for lessons, and a path from assembly lessons to C lessons. Excludes: full real-world ISAs (x86-64, ARM64) for now; showing compiler-generated assembly for C is a possible later lesson. Open design decision recorded in a comment: which instruction set. DoD: the student can type machine code (bytes) and assembly in the IDE, run and single-step it, see registers and memory change, and the same program works in both forms; every behavior has a passing Gherkin spec.
